sam.name: Sam Park
sam.role: engineer (someone who designs and builds things to solve problems)

case.title: Zippy vs Scoot
case.hook: The time capsule is found! Now Rosa needs a second delivery robot for the busy boardwalk. The hot-dog stand next door wants to trade her its robot, Zippy, for Sam’s robot, Scoot. Zippy’s sign makes a big promise. Rosa also has two delivery tickets from this morning.

sign.foot: Trade your old robot today. Ask at the hot-dog stand.

tickets.to: One hot dog to the end of the pier
One cocoa to the lifeguard tower

board.sticky: Zippy went farther. Does that mean Zippy is faster? Should I trade Scoot?

case.question: Which robot is really faster, Zippy or Scoot, and how can we prove it?
case.how: Find 4 clues as you work through the lesson. Then crack the case (solve it) at the top of the Assignment tab.

clues.t: “90 steps” tells how FAR Zippy went, not how FAST. A distance alone can’t prove speed.
To call a race, you need BOTH numbers: how far it went and how long it took.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 2: slice it into seconds
clues.t: In every 10 seconds, Scoot covers 20 steps and Zippy covers 10. More seconds means slower, not faster.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 3: the fair rematch
clues.t: In a fair rematch (same start, same finish, same boardwalk), Scoot took half as long as Zippy.

solve.title: Which robot is really faster?
solve.q: Which answer fits all four clues?

options.t: Zippy. It went 90 steps, more than Scoot’s 60.
options.why: Check Clue 1. Steps tell how far, not how fast.

options.t: Zippy. Its trip lasted 90 seconds, so it ran the longest.
options.why: Check Clue 3. Taking longer means slower, not faster.

options.t: Scoot. Zippy went farther, but it took much longer. In a fair rematch over the same distance, Scoot finished in half the time.
options.why: Case cracked! Speed needs distance AND time, measured in a fair test. Rosa should keep Scoot.

options.t: Nobody can tell. They both look fast when you watch them.
options.why: Check Clue 4. You don’t have to guess: measure the distance and the time.

fixsign.afterText: Does the number on the sign prove that?
fixsign.title: Fix the sign
todo: Read Zippy’s sign. Then read each sentence under it.
Drag a word magnet (a word you can stick on the sign) onto each blank. Or tap a magnet, then tap the blank.
A word that claims too much slides right off.

lines.missAny: Steps are a distance. They tell how far something went.

miss.fast: Steps are a distance. They tell how FAR, not how fast. Fast needs the time, too.

lines.missAny: Compare 90 steps and 60 steps. Which word fits?

miss.faster: Zippy did go more steps. More steps means FARTHER. Faster needs the time, too.

lines.missAny: Does the sign say how long the trip took?

miss.yes: Not so fast! The sign never says how long the trip took.
miss.no: Maybe, maybe not! The sign never says how long the trip took.

fixsign.pickFirst: Pick a word magnet first, then tap the blank.
fixsign.q: What does Zippy’s sign need before it can say FASTEST?

opts.t: How long the trip took: the time.

opts.miss: More steps only means farther. What number is missing?
Fancy letters don’t prove anything! What number is missing?

fixsign.win: A distance alone can’t prove speed. You need the time, too. Clue 1!

scratch.afterText: Call each race before you scratch.
scratch.title: Scratch-off tickets
todo: Read both tickets. Some numbers hide under silver.
Call it first: who is faster?
Scratch off the silver (rub it, or press the button). Then call it again.
scratch.rubTip: Rub the silver with your mouse or finger, or press the button.

rounds.t: The beach dash: Maya vs Jordan

opts1.miss: Maybe! But you can’t see either time yet. Can you be sure?
Maybe! But you can’t see either time yet. Can you be sure?

rounds.line1: Smart! Same distance, but you can’t see either time. Scratch both panels.

opts2.t: Jordan: 10 seconds is more running, so he’s faster.
opts2.miss: More seconds means Jordan took LONGER to go the same 30 feet. Taking longer means slower.
You have both numbers now. Same distance: who took less time?

rounds.line2: Same distance, less time = faster. Maya wins.

rounds.t: Scooter race: Ana vs Ben, 10 seconds each

opts1.miss: Maybe! But you can’t see how far either one went. Can you be sure?
Maybe! But you can’t see how far either one went. Can you be sure?

rounds.line1: Right: same time, but how far did each one go? Scratch to find out.

opts2.miss: Both rode for 10 seconds. Who went more feet in that time?

opts2.t: They tied, because the times match.
opts2.miss: The times match, but the distances don’t. Who went farther in the same time?

rounds.line2: Same time, longer distance = faster. Ana wins.

rounds.t: Zippy vs Scoot: the times were on the back of the tickets!

opts1.miss: That’s the sign’s trick! Steps tell how far, not how fast.
Maybe! But you can’t see the times yet. Can you be sure?

rounds.q2: Both numbers are different now. What do you know for sure?

opts2.t: Zippy went farther, but it also took much longer. I need a fair way to compare.
Zippy is faster. It went more steps.
opts2.miss: More steps means farther. Zippy also took 90 seconds. Is farther the same as faster?

opts2.t: Zippy is faster. It ran for more seconds.
opts2.miss: More seconds means it took LONGER. Is that faster?

rounds.line2: Hold that thought. In Part 2, you’ll slice both runs into pieces to compare them fairly.

scratch.win: Speed needs both numbers: how far it went and how long it took. Clue 2!

slicer.title: Slice it into seconds
todo: Press Run for each robot. Each footprint is one step.
Every 10 seconds the robot stops. Press ✂ Cut (or tap the strip).
Then compare one piece from each robot.

why.t: Zippy and Scoot went different distances in different times. Cutting both runs into pieces of the SAME time lets you compare them fairly.

slicer.compareLabel: One piece from each robot, side by side
slicer.q1: Look at one piece from each robot. Who goes farther in every 10 seconds?

opts1.miss: Look at the two bars. Which piece is longer?
Look at the two bars. Are they the same length?

opts.t: Scoot. In the same time, Scoot goes twice as far.
Zippy. It ran for 90 seconds, so it did more running.
opts.miss: More seconds means it took LONGER. In the same 10 seconds, who went farther?
Farther isn’t faster. Zippy needed 90 seconds for those 90 steps.

slicer.win: Cut both runs into the same amount of time: Scoot covers 20 steps every 10 seconds, Zippy only 10. More seconds means slower. Clue 3!

photofinish.title: The photo-finish camera
todo: Press Run the race.
Watch the photo-finish picture build, one thin slice at a time.
Tap each robot’s nose in that picture to read its time.

why.t: In a close race, a special camera looks only at the finish line. It takes thousands of thin slices every second and lines them up. The picture shows WHEN each racer crossed.

photofinish.sceneAlt: A model race seen from above: a blue robot and an orange robot drive toward a red finish line.
photofinish.stripAlt: The photo-finish picture the model camera builds. Left to right is time, in seconds.
photofinish.preLine: The camera looks through a slit as thin as a hair, right on the red finish line.
photofinish.tapLine: Now tap each robot’s nose in the photo-finish picture: the first moment it touched the line.
photofinish.missTap: Find where {name}’s shape STARTS (its left edge). That is when its nose first touched the line.
photofinish.slowLine: Zippy looks stretched out! It took twice as long to cross the line, because it was slower. Scoot looks squished because it crossed fast. In a photo finish, left to right is TIME, not distance.

photo.alt: A real photo-finish picture of a rowing boat crossing the finish line. The water looks like long stripes and the oars look bent.
photo.cap: A real photo finish from a rowing race in Germany in 2005. The camera saw only the finish line and lined up thousands of thin slices. That is why the water looks like stripes and the oars look bent: they kept moving while the camera scanned. Photo: staff of the 2005 World Rowing Junior Championships, CC BY-SA 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

photofinish.done: Wow! A photo finish measures TIME with a camera. Race officials use it when a race is too close to call by watching.

rematch.afterText: Set the finish, run the race and record your data.
rematch.title: The fair rematch
todo: Drag the 🏁 finish flag onto the tape, or tap a mark.
Press Start the race. Watch both race clocks.
Type each robot’s distance and time into the data table.
Press Check. Your claim builds itself.

why.t: One start line and one finish line for both robots, on the same boardwalk. The only thing that is different is the robot.

rematch.alt: A model race course on the boardwalk: two lanes, one start line and a tape measure marked in steps.
rematch.flagLabel: 🏁 Finish flag: drag me onto the tape, or tap a mark below
rematch.needFlag: Put the finish flag on the tape first.
rematch.distMiss: Check {name}’s distance: where is the finish flag on the tape?
rematch.timeMiss: Check {name}’s time: read its race clock.
rematch.claimLabel: Your claim, built from your table
rematch.claimTpl: I claim that {a} is faster. My data shows {a} went {d} steps in {ta} seconds. {b} took {tb} seconds to go the same {d} steps.
rematch.q: What made this rematch a fair test?

opts.t: Same start, same finish line, same boardwalk. Only the robot was different.

opts.miss: Robots don’t try! What stayed the SAME for both of them?
Watching can fool you. What did we keep the same, and what did we measure?

rematch.win: Same start, same finish, same boardwalk: only the robot changed. Scoot took half the time. Clue 4!

headstart.title: Zippy’s owner has a video
todo: Press Play. Zippy’s owner says this race proves Zippy is faster.
Tap the part of the replay that isn’t fair.
Then run a fair redo.
headstart.alt: A model replay of a two-lane robot race with a red finish line.
headstart.caption: 🌭 ZIPPY WINS! (says Zippy’s owner)
headstart.spotQ: Something about this race isn’t fair. Tap it in the replay.

spots.miss: Both robots had the same finish line. Look at where each robot STARTED.

headstart.spotLine: Zippy started 20 steps closer to the finish! Scoot had to go 30 steps. Zippy only went 10.

opts.t: No. They didn’t start at the same line, so it wasn’t a fair test.
Yes. Zippy crossed the finish line first.
opts.miss: Crossing first isn’t the same as being faster. Did they both go the same distance?

headstart.fairLine: Same start line this time: Scoot crosses in 15 seconds. Zippy needs 30. A head start can make a slower robot look faster.
headstart.win: Twist solved! Only a fair test counts.

hlCoach.title: Highlight like a scientist
tips: Highlight key words, not whole paragraphs.
If everything is yellow, nothing stands out. Aim for a few words in each paragraph.
Look for words that are explained.
Bold words, and words followed by “means”, “is called” or a meaning in ( ), are often worth saving.
Look for answers to the Big Question.
Ask yourself: does this help me tell how far, how long or who was faster?
“Because”, “so” and “first … then” show how ideas connect.
Yellow = important. Green = evidence I might use in my answer. Pink = something I wonder about.

practice.q: Practice: tap the 3 to 5 words that matter most in this sentence.
practice.text: Speed needs two numbers: how far something went and how long it took.
practice.model: A scientist might highlight “speed”, “far” and “long”. Those words hold the big idea.

hlCoach.outside: This works in every subject. When you read anything, save the words that answer your question, and skip the rest.
